name: Commodity hedging pressure (CFTC positions)

origin.source_title: Capturing the risk premium of commodity futures: the role of hedging pressure (Journal of Banking and Finance 37(7), 2013)

how_it_works.simple: Use the weekly government report of who holds commodity futures. Buy where producers are hedging heavily (they pay others to take the risk), sell where consumers are.
how_it_works.analogy: Like an insurer charging more when many people want cover at once.
how_it_works.precise: Hedging pressure = hedgers' net short positions over their total positions (CFTC Commitments of Traders). Long the commodities with the most net-short hedgers, short those with the most net-long; single and double sorts with speculators' positions.

rule: Monthly: from CFTC legacy reports, hedging pressure = (commercial short - commercial long) / (commercial short + long), averaged over 52 weeks; long top third, short bottom third.
data_needed: CFTC Commitments of Traders, weekly, free
economic_rationale: Keynesian normal backwardation: hedgers pay a premium to speculators who take the other side.
why_it_might_fail: Gorton, Hayashi and Rouwenhorst (2013) reject hedging pressure as a determinant of premia; results vary across studies; the reported Sharpe ratio is gross.

reported_results.source: Miffre's literature review, as summarised by CXO Advisory
reported_results.notes: Average gross Sharpe ratio of hedging-pressure portfolios in the review; we did not read the review itself.

relevance.reason: Free data, but mixed evidence; low priority.
